name: Question 45
problem:
The following table shows the number of customers per minute, $C(t),$ that arrive at a bank, measured over a period of $15$ minutes.

| $t\,\text{(minutes)}$ | $0$ | $3$ | $7$ | $12$ | $15$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $C(t)\,\text{(customers/minute)}$ | $3$ | $4$ | $3$ | $5$ | $2$ |

Use the right Riemann sum over $[0,15]$ with four subintervals to approximate the total number of customers served.
worked_solution:
Let $A$ denote the area under the curve $y=C(t)$ over $[0,15].$ In this case, we have $n=4$ rectangles. Using the right Riemann sum, the area is approximated as 

$$
A≈C(3)Δ{t}_{1}+C(7)Δ{t}_{2}+C(12)Δ{t}_{3}+C(15)Δ{t}_{4},
$$

where each $Δ{t}_{i}$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $t$-value and the previous one, i.e.,

$$
Δ{t}_{i}={t}_{i}-{t}_{i-1}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $Δt$'s.

| $t$ | $0$ | $3$ | $7$ | $12$ | $15$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Δt$ | $-$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $3$ |
| $C(t)$ | $-$ | $4$ | $3$ | $5$ | $2$ |

We plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈4\cdot 3+3\cdot 4+5\cdot 5+2\cdot 3 \\  & =12+12+25+6 \\  & =55.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total number of customers served over a period of $15$ minutes. So, the total number of customers is approximately
$55.$
